insight.title: Why You Find New Problems After Solving Old Ones
insight.subtitle: How your brain creates stress even when things are going well

sections.text: Have you noticed that life gets easier, but your stress stays the same? Your brain has a hidden system for finding trouble. As big problems vanish, your mind simply lowers its standards for "problems."

When actual threats disappear, your mind lowers its threshold for what qualifies as a crisis. You don’t necessarily have more trouble; you’ve simply expanded your definition of it to keep your brain occupied.
This explains why a slight delay or a minor critique feels like a disaster on an otherwise perfect day. We often mistake a calm environment for a new set of emergencies that aren’t there.
When you notice a minor annoyance today, ask if it's a real problem or just a perception shift.
High standards for your life should not require a low threshold for your peace of mind.

news.title: AIIMS and GMPSF Host 16th India Probiotic Symposium, Spotlighting Gut Health's Growing Role in Preventive Healthcare
news.description: New Delhi [India], April 7: The All-India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), in collaboration with the Gut Microbiota and Probiotic Science Foundation (India), hosted the 16th India Probiotic Symposium on March 27-28, 2026 at the Jawaharlal Nehru Auditorium, AIIMS, New Delhi. The symposium, themed 'Gut Microbiome and Probiotics: Impact from Cradle to Centenarians,' brought together leading clinicians, researchers and global experts, to deliberate on the expanding role of microbiome science, in preventive and clinical healthcare.

news.title: This new chip survives 1300°F (700°C) and could change AI forever
news.description: A team of engineers has created a breakthrough memory device that keeps working at temperatures hotter than molten lava, shattering one of electronics’ biggest limits. Built from an unusual stack of ultra-durable materials, the tiny component can store data and perform calculations even at 700°C (1300°F), far beyond what today’s chips can handle. The discovery was partly accidental, but it revealed a powerful new mechanism that prevents heat-induced failure at the atomic level.
